title: Microsoft Teams: admin recommendations to enable agents and apps for applications already in use
summary: The briefing accurately reports Microsoft's optional, administrator-enabled recommendations and distinguishes the rollout notice from the roadmap target. The documented app-management paths and PowerShell commands are supported, and the feature-specific documentation and licensing gaps remain appropriately qualified.

claims.claim: Per-app availability is edited in Teams admin center under Teams apps > Manage apps > app > Users and groups > Availability > Edit availability.
claims.quote:
Search for the required app and select the app name to open its app details page.
3. Select the **Users and groups** tab.
4. Under **Select to manage who this app is installed for or available to in your organization**, select **Availability**.
5. Select **Edit availability**.

claims.where: controls[1].api; Governance controls table and prose
claims.claim: MicrosoftTeams PowerShell command Update-M365TeamsApp -Id <app ID> -AppAssignmentType Everyone sets app availability to Everyone.
claims.quote:
Update-M365TeamsApp -Id 4c4ec2e8-4a2c-4bce-8d8f-00fc664a4e5b -AppAssignmentType Everyone
```

Updates the availability value for Bookings app (App ID 4c4ec2e8-4a2c-4bce-8d8f-00fc664a4e5b) to Everyone.

claims.where: controls[2].ui; Governance guidance; Governance controls table
claims.claim: The bulk third-party app control is in Teams admin center under Teams apps > Manage apps > Actions > Org-wide app settings > Third-party apps.
claims.quote:
On **Manage apps** page, under the **Actions** menu, select **Org-wide app settings**. You can then configure the settings in the pane.
Under **Third-party apps**, a single control manages the bulk availability of both the new and existing third-party agents and apps.

claims.claim: No PowerShell cmdlet or equivalent API for the org-wide Third-party apps toggle is documented.
claims.quote: Searched: "Teams" "org-wide" "third-party" "PowerShell"; "Teams" "org-wide app settings" "API". Read manage-apps, app-centric-management and Set-CsTeamsClientConfiguration syntax excerpts; no automation equivalent for this toggle found.

claims.claim: Learn specifies the Teams Administrator role for using Teams admin center.
claims.quote: To use Teams admin center, you must have a Teams Administrator role. Some admins with a higher privilege role can accomplish agent and app governance tasks but we recommend using the lower privilege role where possible.

claims.claim: Before unified app management migration, apps and agents must be allowed in both Teams admin center and Microsoft 365 admin center's Integrated apps page.
claims.quote: If your organization isn't migrated to unified app management, allow apps and Copilot agents in Teams admin center and under the **Integrated apps** page in Microsoft 365 admin center.

claims.claim: After unified app management migration, either admin center can be used to allow apps and agents.
claims.quote: If your organization is migrated to unified app management, allow apps and Copilot agents in Teams admin center or under the **Integrated apps** page in Microsoft 365 admin center.

claims.claim: Everyone availability includes all organization users, new users and guests.
claims.quote: `Everyone` | Available to all org users, new users, and guests.

claims.claim: Specific users or groups availability limits app use to selected users and groups.
claims.quote: `Specific users or groups` | Only the users and groups that you select can use the app.

claims.claim: Guests cannot use an app assigned through Specific users or groups, even if assigned.
claims.quote: Guests can't use the app if this option is selected and even if guests are assigned to the app.

claims.quote: In the terms of use and privacy policy of any agent or app, the app developer discloses what data their agent or app uses and how it handles the data.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Change & support; Open questions
claims.claim: Learn states that third-party agents and apps are blocked by default in GCC, GCC High and DoD.
claims.quote: In a Microsoft 365 Government - GCC, GCCH and DoD deployment of Teams, all third-party agents and apps are blocked by default.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Change & support; Open questions
claims.claim: Microsoft has not explained how recommendations interact with GCC's default block on third-party apps.
claims.quote: Searched: "Teams" "recommendations" "existing applications" "GCC" "prerequisites". Read MC1481316 and learn.microsoft.com/microsoftteams/manage-apps and /app-centric-management; GCC rollout is listed but interaction with the government default block is not explained.

claims.claim: Learn documents an existing Popular apps in your org widget on the Manage apps page.
claims.quote: In Teams admin center, the **Popular apps in your org** widget on the **Manage apps** page displays two of the most-used third-party apps, that aren't already available or installed for everyone in the organization.

claims.claim: The sources do not establish the relationship between the existing Popular apps widget and this new recommendations feature.
claims.quote: Searched: Teams manage apps Popular apps in your org widget; "Teams" "recommendations" "existing applications". Read app-centric-management's View top apps insights section, manage-apps and MC1481316; none identifies the widget as this roadmap feature.

claims.claim: Under app-centric management, org-wide settings apply to new apps and existing apps whose availability was not actively managed.
claims.quote:
The Org-wide app settings apply to:

- All the new apps made available in Teams app store.
- All the existing apps that you didn't actively manage, that is, you didn't change the availability of.
